skill.name: pwdebug
skill.description: Control a real Chromium browser from the command line for frontend debugging, page inspection, screenshots, and console log review.
skill.summary: Command-line Playwright debugging for live Chromium sessions.
skill.author: DCjanus

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate Playwright browser debugging CLI, but it launches a persistent Chromium process with CDP access. Most static hits in SKILL.md and picker.py are false positives from Markdown fences, JavaScript template literals, or keyboard event names. Safer defaults and clearer warnings are needed for CDP exposure, local artifacts, and page script evaluation.

remediation.issue: Persistent Chromium process exposes a local CDP control surface.
remediation.suggestion: Use a random local port by default, document the trust boundary, and clear state when the service stops.

remediation.issue: Extra browser arguments are accepted without restriction.
remediation.suggestion: Validate or allowlist high-risk flags, and explain that arguments can weaken browser isolation.

remediation.issue: Console logs, state, profiles, and screenshots can persist sensitive data locally.
remediation.suggestion: Set restrictive directory permissions, add cleanup commands, and warn users before logging sensitive pages.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary JavaScript can run in the active page context.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before evaluating JavaScript on authenticated or production pages.

semantic_findings.description: The start command launches Chromium with a remote debugging port and records the endpoint. Any local process that reaches the port can inspect and control that debug browser.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The browser arguments include a remote debugging port and a persistent user data directory. The endpoint is written to local state after startup.

content.user_title: Debug Browser Pages from the Command Line
content.value_statement: Frontend debugging often needs a real browser session that survives across commands. This skill provides Playwright-based browser control for navigation, inspection, screenshots, and logs.
actual_capabilities: Starts a Chromium browser service through Playwright and CDP.
Navigates the active page to a requested URL.
Evaluates JavaScript expressions in the current browser page.
Captures full-page or viewport screenshots to a local temporary file.
Injects an element picker that returns selected DOM element details.
Records console messages and page errors for later review.
limitations: Only Chromium is supported in the current implementation.
Requires uv, Playwright, and an installed Chromium browser.
Stores browser state and console logs on the local filesystem.
Does not replace a full automated browser test framework.

use_cases.title: Inspect a Broken Frontend Flow
use_cases.description: Open a page, run focused JavaScript checks, capture a screenshot, and review console errors in one browser session.

use_cases.title: Collect Reproduction Evidence
use_cases.description: Navigate to a reported issue, save visual evidence, and gather browser console messages for a bug report.

use_cases.title: Guide an AI Coding Session
use_cases.description: Let an assistant inspect page state and selected elements while working on UI fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Debug Browser
prompt_templates.prompt: Start pwdebug in headed mode, open my local app, and confirm that the page title loads.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Page Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pwdebug to open this URL, capture a full-page screenshot, and summarize visible layout problems.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect an Element
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the element picker to select the login button and report its text, classes, and parent structure.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Console Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Watch console logs while reproducing the issue, then review the latest entries and identify likely frontend causes.

output_examples.input: Start the browser service and open a development page.
output_examples.output: The service starts, reports a local CDP endpoint, and opens the requested page in Chromium.

output_examples.input: Pick the sign-in button on the current page.
output_examples.output: The result lists the selected element tag, text, classes, short HTML preview, and parent structure.

output_examples.input: Review the latest console messages after reproducing a bug.
output_examples.output: The output shows recent log levels, messages, timestamps, and source locations when available.

best_practices: Use a dedicated test browser profile for debugging sessions.
Stop the browser service when the debugging task is complete.
Clear saved logs and screenshots when they may contain sensitive data.
anti_patterns: Do not run arbitrary page JavaScript on sensitive production accounts.
Do not expose the CDP port beyond localhost.
Do not leave persistent debug sessions running unattended.

faq.question: What browser does this skill control?
faq.answer: It controls Chromium through Playwright and the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

faq.question: Can it reuse the same browser across commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It writes local state so later commands can reconnect to the running browser service.

faq.question: Where are logs stored?
faq.answer: Console logs are stored under the local pwdebug cache directory in the user home folder.

faq.question: Does it support screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. It can save viewport or full-page screenshots to a temporary local file.

faq.question: Is arbitrary JavaScript evaluation supported?
faq.answer: Yes. Treat this as a trusted debugging action because it runs in the active page context.

faq.question: Is this a complete test runner?
faq.answer: No. It is a debugging helper for live browser inspection, not a full test automation suite.
